top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards a new organising concept: Kane and Mele's Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant, spin-orbit-coupled insulators with protected edge states, and Molenkamp's observation of the edge channels in HgTe wells. It is a prediction followed by a direct experimental test, stable for over fifteen years across many materials, and the joint Kane-Mele work makes the three-name allocation coherent. The gaps (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan's 3D work) and the 2016 overlap are real but can be handled by a narrow citation on the Z2 invariant and time-reversal-symmetric edge physics. P001 is a mature, well-attributed two-name invention, with the magic-wavelength lattice separating it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, but it is a measurement capability rather than new physics, so I rank it second, above no award.
